criteria.name: Secrets handling
criteria.rationale: The app needs no credentials, none appear in source, image or logs, and registry access used doctl's own login flow without printing tokens. .env is excluded via .gitignore/.dockerignore.

criteria.name: Deployment provenance
criteria.rationale: The image was built locally from the reviewed source with zero npm dependencies and pushed to an owner-controlled DOCR registry, but the base image node:22-alpine is not digest-pinned, the deployed tag v1 is mutable, and doctl was installed from a GitHub tarball without checksum verification.

criteria.name: Terms compliance
criteria.rationale: Commercial use on a paid App Platform basic instance ($5/mo, always-on, not sleeping) plus a free starter registry tier, both of which allow commercial use under DigitalOcean's standard terms. The account plan wasn't readable, so this assumes a normal paid account.

criteria.name: Least privilege
criteria.rationale: Single App Platform service running as the non-root 'node' user, no database or extra public resources, and the CSV is baked read-only into the image. Minor: the registry login was left at the default 30-day credential lifetime on the build host.

criteria.name: Transport security
criteria.rationale: HTTPS works with a valid Google Trust Services certificate and HTTP returns a 301 redirect to HTTPS, but the app sets no HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection or CSP headers even though it could easily add them.

criteria.name: Attack surface
criteria.rationale: Only the three static files and the API/health routes are served through an explicit allowlist. Probes for .env, .git/config, package.json, source, the CSV, the Dockerfile and path traversal all returned 404/400 with no stack traces.

criteria.name: Application security
criteria.rationale: Inputs are validated (dates by regex, filters by exact match, limit capped at 500), non-GET methods are rejected, errors are generic, and the client escapes all data before using innerHTML. Missing: CSP/security headers and any application-level rate limiting, and Date.parse accepts impossible dates such as 2025-02-31.

findings.title: Base image not pinned by digest
findings.recommendation: Pin the base image by digest (node:22-alpine@sha256:...) and update it on purpose.

findings.title: Mutable image tag deployed; built from an ad-hoc workstation, not CI
findings.evidence: app/.do/app.yaml: image tag 'v1'; process/deploy.md: docker build ... && docker push registry.digitalocean.com/adb-6mbv0-dataviz/adb-6mbv0-dataviz-web:v1 (digest sha256:97c7c564...)
findings.recommendation: Deploy by immutable digest or unique per-commit tags, ideally built by CI from a repository the owner controls.

findings.title: doctl downloaded without checksum verification
findings.evidence: process/deploy.md: curl -sL https://github.com/digitalocean/doctl/releases/download/v1.146.0/doctl-1.146.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz | tar xz && sudo mv doctl /usr/local/bin/ (doctl was already installed, so this branch did not run)
findings.recommendation: Verify the release checksum or install from a trusted package source.

findings.title: No security headers (HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, CSP)
findings.evidence: curl -sI https://adb-6mbv0-dataviz-dyatk.ondigitalocean.app/ returns only content-type, cache-control and platform headers; app/src/server.js send() sets only Content-Type and Cache-Control
findings.recommendation: Add Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors and a restrictive Content-Security-Policy in send().

findings.title: Registry credential left at the 30-day default
findings.evidence: process/deploy.md: doctl registry login -> 'Login valid for 30 days'
findings.recommendation: Use --expiry-seconds for short-lived registry logins on build hosts.

findings.title: No application-level rate limiting on public API
findings.evidence: app/src/server.js: /api/summary and /api/orders have no throttling; GET /api/orders?limit=99999 returned 500 rows (capped)
findings.recommendation: Rely on platform/Cloudflare protections or add simple per-IP rate limiting; the cap on limit already bounds the cost of each response.

findings.title: Impossible calendar dates accepted
findings.evidence: GET /api/summary?start=2025-02-31 returned 200 with filtered data; app/src/data.js parseFilters uses DATE_RE plus Date.parse, which rolls dates over
findings.recommendation: Round-trip the date through toISOString().slice(0,10) and reject it if the result differs.

security.summary: A zero-dependency Node.js dashboard running as a non-root container on a paid DigitalOcean App Platform instance, with no secrets involved, a strict static-file allowlist, validated inputs and escaped client rendering. HTTPS and the HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect work correctly. The weaknesses are minor: the base image isn't digest-pinned, the deployed image tag is mutable and was pushed from a workstation, and the app sends no security headers (HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, CSP).

final_messages.build:
The sales dashboard is built and works locally: the 5 automated tests pass, and I checked every requirement with curl and a screenshot of the page. The servers and the test Docker container are stopped.

**Stack:** plain Node.js (version 20 or later) with no npm packages to install. The server loads `data/sales.csv` into memory when it starts and listens on `$PORT` (default 8080), so it fits DigitalOcean App Platform as a Node.js app or as a Docker container.

**Dashboard (`GET /`):**
- Filters for region, category and a from/to date range sit above the charts.
- Three KPI tiles show total revenue, orders and units sold.
- Two hand-drawn bar charts show revenue by month and revenue by category, with hover tooltips.
- The orders table shows 50 rows at a time, newest first, with Newer/Older buttons.
- Changing a filter updates everything without reloading the page.

**`GET /api/summary`:**
- Returns exactly the format in the spec, with the filters combined with AND and both dates included.
- Revenue is summed in whole cents and then rounded to 2 decimals, so totals don't pick up floating-point errors.
- When nothing matches, it returns zeros and empty arrays.
- I added one thing the spec didn't ask for: a malformed date gets a `400` error instead of being ignored.

Unfiltered, it reports $1,839,455.69 from 2,400 orders and 15,179 units.

I also added three endpoints the page uses: `/api/orders` (for the table, with `limit` and `offset`), `/api/options` (the filter choices) and `/healthz` (a health check).

**Files:** the server is in `src/server.js` and `src/data.js`, the page in `public/`, and the tests in `test/api.test.js`. There's also a `Dockerfile` and a `README.md`.

**To run it:**
- `npm start`, then open http://localhost:8080
- `npm test` runs the tests.
- `docker build -t sales-dashboard . && docker run -p 8080:8080 sales-dashboard` runs it in a container; I built and started it this way, and the health check responded.
final_messages.deploy:
The dashboard is live at **https://adb-6mbv0-dataviz-dyatk.ondigitalocean.app**, and every `TASK.md` requirement checked out through that URL. Nothing needed a person to step in.

**What I deployed:**
- **Container Registry** `adb-6mbv0-dataviz` on the free starter tier. The app's Docker image `adb-6mbv0-dataviz-web:v1` is stored there.
- **App Platform app** `adb-6mbv0-dataviz`, running one service, `adb-6mbv0-dataviz-web`, on the smallest paid size (`apps-s-1vcpu-0.5gb`) in New York. The settings are in `.do/app.yaml`. HTTPS comes from App Platform's default `ondigitalocean.app` address, and `/healthz` is the health check.
- **Estimated cost:** about $5/month, all for the app service; the registry is free.

**Checked through the public URL:**
- The dashboard page and its files load.
- `/api/summary` returns the same results as locally: unfiltered totals, a combined region + category + date filter, and zeros with empty arrays when nothing matches.
- `/api/orders` returns filtered, paginated rows.
- A screenshot of the live page with the Software filter applied shows the KPIs, both charts and the table all updated.

**Before you deploy a new version:** build and push a new image tag, change the tag in `.do/app.yaml`, then run `doctl apps update 77d60e13-3186-4272-aa75-443bd5b1ae15 --spec .do/app.yaml`.

I didn't create any credentials, so there's no `.env`. I added `.env` to `.gitignore` and `.dockerignore` anyway. The resource details are in `deployment.json`.
